title: Track the lore-generated bundle index and log
description: The bundle generates three files this repository does not track: the lore-managed index block sync writes into docs/index.md, and docs/adr/index.md and docs/log.md, which sync creates. The split state is actively broken rather than merely untidy: committing the block without the files it links breaks the Docs job on a clean checkout, measured here on 2026-09-28 as lore check --strict exit 6 with a broken-link report for adr/index.md. Ruled by opum-agent the same day: track them; do not configure lore out of generating them. Independently verified by ref here before implementing (a relayed measurement is not one of mine): docs/index.md and docs/log.md are tracked on origin/dev in all six sibling repositories read (opum-agent, opum-doc, lore-cli, quest-cli, opum-fleet, opum-cli-e2e), and docs/adr/index.md in the four of those that have an ADR directory. Land as its own docs PR, separately from task work; read the whole generated diff before committing rather than git add -A, because lore has been reported to truncate docs/log.md on regeneration (opum-cli-e2e LCLI-474 as relayed to this session, not verified here) and an unread regeneration is exactly where that would land unnoticed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The generated files are tracked and committed in a state lore check --strict accepts (exit 0), and the Docs CI job is green on a clean checkout of that state - the case that fails today when the index block is committed without them

The committed index files are exactly what lore regenerates: a second lore sync over the committed tree produces no diff in docs/index.md or docs/adr/index.md. No committed log entry names a commit unreachable from origin/dev - branch-only commits are excluded, because a squash merge leaves them unreachable there and the next rebuild drops them

plan: 2. Run lore sync; read the whole generated diff, docs/log.md in full, before staging anything.
3. Commit the tracked generated files, confirm lore validate --strict and lore check --strict exit 0 and a second sync is a no-op.
4. PR, CI green including Docs on a clean checkout, squash merge, delete the local branch.
implementationNotes: MEASUREMENT (2026-09-28, before committing): lore derives docs/log.md from HEAD-inclusive history, so the commit that adds a log entry is itself always the next entry - a fixed point is unreachable, and I disproved my own first wording of the second criterion ('a second sync produces no diff') three ways: an amend (entry for the amended commit appeared), a log-only commit (entry for the log-only commit appeared), and the sibling check that the fleet's own logs lag HEAD. lore check --strict exits 0 with the log one entry behind (measured), so currency of the log is not gated. What I commit therefore is the log as derivable from dev-reachable history: the branch's own commits are excluded because they never land on dev (the PR is squash-merged), and a log entry naming an unreachable SHA would be dropped by the next rebuild anyway. The index files are committed exactly as regenerated; they are the part a stale copy actually breaks.

CRITERION REFINED A SECOND TIME, reason recorded: my first wording ('a second sync produces no diff') was disproved as unreachable; the second ('entries derivable from history reachable at HEAD') was still imprecise, because on the branch HEAD is a branch-only commit that a squash merge will drop, so a literal reading would demand committing an entry for a SHA that cannot exist on dev. The committed criterion is the one actually verified: no sync diff in the index files, and every committed log SHA reachable from origin/dev.
finalSummary: Landed as docs/WCLI-28-track-lore-generated-index-log, PR opum-ai/ward-cli#31, CI run 36497784927 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green on df02846, the head this closes on). WHAT: the three files the lore bundle generates are now tracked - the lore:index block in docs/index.md, docs/adr/index.md and docs/log.md - so a docs change plus lore sync no longer leaves a dirty tree whose committed half breaks CI. WHY IT WAS BROKEN RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: measured before the change, committing the index block without the files it links makes the Docs job fail on a clean checkout (lore check --strict exit 6, link adr/index.md not in the bundle). RULING AND ITS INDEPENDENT CHECK: opum-agent ruled to track them as the fleet convention; verified here by ref before implementing, not taken on relay - docs/index.md and docs/log.md exist on origin/dev in all six sibling repositories read, and docs/adr/index.md in the four with an ADR directory. VERIFIED: lore validate --strict exit 0 and lore check --strict exit 0 on the committed tree (the case that exited 6 before); a second lore sync over the committed tree produces no diff in docs/index.md or docs/adr/index.md; all seven committed log SHAs were checked as ancestors of origin/dev in the same invocation, so no committed entry names an unreachable commit; and the Docs job is green on the PR's own clean checkout, which is the failing case itself. THE LOG'S LIMIT, MEASURED AND RECORDED: lore derives docs/log.md from HEAD-inclusive history, so the commit that adds an entry is always the next pending one and a fixed point is unreachable - measured three ways (an amend, a log-only commit, and the fleet's own logs lagging HEAD). lore check exits 0 with the log one entry behind, so log currency is not gated; branch-only commits are deliberately excluded from the committed log because a squash merge leaves them unreachable, where the next rebuild would drop them. Every generated file was read in full before staging, deliberately not git add -A, because a relayed report says lore has truncated docs/log.md elsewhere (LCLI-474; not verified here).
